recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-6310 unless Pharmacy reopens the broader MedicationStatement status/adherence model in a new tracker.
issue_request: Published Pharmacy change request with resolution Persuasive with Modification asking for a MedicationStatementStatus value for medications planned for future use, because DSTU1 forced those statements into in-process. The final resolution broadened the work to reviewing and updating all statuses from the Pharmacy status spreadsheet.
initial_application: Jira cites svn 6552. Git commit d3c2a3a0552f97b710394710badf5ee4e69c0d56 is svn 6552 and changed MedicationStatement.status from in-progress | completed | entered-in-error to a Pharmacy spreadsheet status set. Commit 31e9678a6e9f698b2828df5d58dc739aad32c602 immediately refined that work to active | completed | entered-in-error | intended and described status as the state of the medication used, so planned future use was historically represented by intended.
additional_context: MedicationStatement remains active in source/fhir.ini. Later published Pharmacy decisions changed the model: FHIR-19468 and FHIR-19470 moved taking/not-taking semantics into adherence, FHIR-32060 redesigned status to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft, FHIR-39271 confirmed status is about recording the statement rather than the underlying medication, and FHIR-38682 renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while preserving the later status/adherence model. Current narrative still says MedicationStatement can record medications planned for future use.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-adding a planned or intended status code would conflict with the later final status/adherence design; current build-scope source already supports future-use statements through resource scope, effective timing, and adherence while keeping status as recorded | entered-in-error | draft.

related_jiras.note: Another DSTU1 MedicationStatement status issue whose combined-branch audit identifies the same svn 6552 Pharmacy status-spreadsheet application.
Another status-semantics issue fixed as part of FHIR-6310/svn 6552 and already audited on the combined branch.
svn 6553 immediately refined the FHIR-6310 application by correcting MedicationStatement.status description and codes.
Moved taking/not-taking semantics out of status and into adherence.
Added the adherence attribute that carries taking/not-taking behavior.
Redesigned MedicationStatement/MedicationUsage status to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft.
Renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while preserving the later status/adherence changes.
Confirmed status is the recording status of the statement and adherence represents medication being taken or not taken.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking for MedicationStatementStatus support for planned future medications, with resolution to review and update all statuses.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the approved request and points to svn 6552 as the historical application.

evidence_items.summary: svn 6552 applied FHIR-6310's Pharmacy status-spreadsheet update, and svn 6553 refined MedicationStatement.status to active, completed, entered-in-error, and intended.
evidence_items.learned: The planned-future request was historically applied in the old MedicationStatement status model.

evidence_items.summary: MedicationStatement is active, status is recorded | entered-in-error | draft, and the narrative still says the resource covers planned future use.
evidence_items.learned: The current source preserves future-use scope while intentionally using the later recording-status model.

evidence_items.summary: Later Published Pharmacy decisions redesigned MedicationStatement status as statement-recording status and kept the later model when MedicationUsage was renamed back.
evidence_items.learned: These later final decisions supersede restoring a planned/intended status code today.

evidence_items.summary: A 2019-2022 thread discussed confusion between active/intended/completed status, effectivePeriod, and adherence; Jean Duteau said R5 fixed this by using recorded, draft, and entered-in-error status plus effectivePeriod and adherence.
evidence_items.learned: Community discussion supports the later redesign that makes a new planned status inappropriate now.

evidence_items.summary: Participants confirmed future-use MedicationStatement scenarios while discussing their boundary with MedicationRequest.
evidence_items.learned: Future-use MedicationStatement scope remains valid even without a dedicated status code.

evidence_items.summary: Pharmacy minutes record discussion of MedicationUsage name/status/adherence and a vote to revert the resource name to MedicationStatement.
evidence_items.learned: Formal WG context aligns with keeping the later status/adherence model rather than restoring old status values.
